Quick answers to the questions I hear most. If yours isn't here, email
[hi@rumizi.com](mailto:hi@rumizi.com) and I'll add it.

## Getting set up

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="How long does it take to get a menu live?">
    If you already have your menu as a photo, PDF, or web page, you can
    have a publishable draft in about ten minutes. Walk-through:
    [Set up your first menu](/vendors/first-menu).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Do I need to install an app?">
    No. Rumizi runs in the browser on any device. You'll mostly use it
    from a laptop to build the menu, then a phone or tablet to tweak
    things at the venue.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="How do diners scan my menu?">
    Any phone camera app scans a QR code. There's no Rumizi app to
    install. You print the QR once and put it on tables.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Can I use my own domain?">
    Not yet — custom domains like `menu.yourvenue.com` are on the
    roadmap. You do get two Rumizi addresses today, though:
    `rumizi.com/your-venue` and `your-venue.rumizi.com`. Both work; the
    subdomain redirects to the path version, which is the canonical one
    to print on a QR code.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="What do diners see first — the menu or the chat?">
    The chat, at most venues. Your public link opens the AI assistant
    with the full menu one tap away in the header. If you'd rather it
    opened the menu directly, email me and I'll switch the chat off for
    your venue.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Menus and editing

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Can I have more than one menu?">
    Yes — most venues have at least *Lunch* and *Dinner*. Each menu has
    its own items, photos, and [open hours](/vendors/menu/scheduling).
    The menu with an active schedule window is what diners see by
    default; when no schedule matches, the venue's public link opens
    the **first** menu in your Menus list, so drag the one you want at
    the front to the top. See [Edit your menu](/vendors/menu/editing).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Do I have to publish every small change?">
    Content edits (names, prices, descriptions, photos) need a publish
    before diners see them. Availability changes (out of stock, back in
    stock) are live immediately.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="I published by mistake. How do I roll back?">
    In the menu editor, tap **Revert last publish**. The previous
    snapshot is restored and diners see it on the next page load.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Can I preview changes before publishing?">
    Yes. Open `rumizi.com/your-venue/menu?menu=<menu-id>` — as a
    signed-in owner or staff member, you'll see the working copy instead
    of the published one. Signed out, the same link shows the published
    copy, so it's safe to share. Details:
    [Publish and preview](/vendors/menu/publish).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="How do I mark an item out of stock?">
    Open the item, pick a mode: *indefinite*, *until tomorrow*, or
    *until the next open window*. Changes are live immediately — no
    publish. Details: [Availability and stock](/vendors/menu/availability).
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## AI features

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="How good is the AI menu extraction?">
    Very good for clear photos and well-structured PDFs. Blurry phone
    shots of laminated menus are still readable but need more cleanup.
    You always review before publishing, so there's no risk of wrong
    data going live.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Can the AI assistant see my menu?">
    Yes — it reads your menu, schedules, tags, and settings, and can
    edit them only with your explicit **Apply change** confirmation.
    Details: [Rumizi Assistant](/vendors/assistant/overview).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Can diners talk to an AI assistant?">
    Yes. There's a separate diner-facing assistant that answers questions
    about your menu — allergens, spice level, pairings, "what's good
    for two". It's a pure advisor: it recommends dishes but never
    places an order. Details:
    [Menu assistant for diners](/diners/menu-assistant).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Which AI features need a paid plan?">
    The diner-facing menu assistant, the workspace Rumizi Assistant, and
    AI image generation all need **Pro AI** or **Max AI**. AI menu
    extraction — reading a photo or PDF into a draft menu — works on
    every plan, including Always Free.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="I don't want AI at all. Can I turn it off?">
    Yes. Email [hi@rumizi.com](mailto:hi@rumizi.com) and I'll disable
    the assistant for your venue even on a paid plan. Manual editing
    works identically.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Do diners see what I write in the assistant context?">
    Only the **item**-level notes. Venue, menu, and category context is
    read by the AI but never shown. Item context also renders on the
    item card and detail page, so write it for a guest to read. Details:
    [Edit your menu](/vendors/menu/editing#briefing-the-diner-assistant).
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Languages

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="How many languages can I offer?">
    Rumizi supports ten today: English, Spanish, Italian, Arabic, Hindi,
    Persian, French, Chinese, Punjabi, and Tagalog. You can enable as
    many as you want.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="What if I don't translate every item?">
    Missing translations fall back to your default language. Diners
    never see a blank name or description.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Billing

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="How much does Rumizi cost?">
    Your menu is free forever. Two paid plans lift the assistant on:
    **Pro AI** at \$199/month or \$1,990/year answers up to 50 guests a
    day, and **Max AI** at \$499/month or \$4,990/year answers up to 150.
    All in USD. Above 150 a day, write to
    [hello@rumizi.com](mailto:hello@rumizi.com). See
    [Plans and billing](/vendors/billing/subscription).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="What's actually free?">
    **Always Free** is your whole digital menu, forever: unlimited
    menus, unlimited categories, unlimited dishes, your QR code with no
    scan limits, and your own domain. What it doesn't include is the
    AI — no menu assistant for your diners, no AI image generation, no
    workspace copilot. AI menu extraction (reading a photo or PDF into
    a draft menu) works on Free too.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="What happens when my trial ends?">
    Your venue moves to **Always Free**. Nothing is blocked and nothing
    is deleted — your menu stays live and scannable, every dish still
    on it. You lose the assistant, AI image generation, and the
    workspace copilot. Subscribe at any point and everything comes
    straight back.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="How long is the free trial?">
    **Two calendar months** of Pro AI, without a card. Sign up on the
    15th, the trial ends on the 15th.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="How do I cancel?">
    Email [hi@rumizi.com](mailto:hi@rumizi.com). I'll cancel and confirm
    with you. In-app cancellation is on the roadmap.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Can I get a refund if it's not right for me?">
    Yes — if your guests don't use it, don't pay. Email me in the first
    month and I'll sort it out personally.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Staff and access

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="How do I invite staff?">
    From your workspace, open **More → Staff** and invite them. They sign
    in passwordlessly like you do — no password to share.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="What can staff do?">
    Staff can edit menus, mark items out of stock, and manage open hours.
    Billing, staff management, venue settings, and slug changes stay
    owner-only.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="How do I sign in?">
    Go to `rumizi.com/login` and give an email address or phone number.
    You'll get a one-time code to type in; by email you also get a magic
    link. Open the link, then tap **Sign in** on the page it lands on to
    finish — opening the link alone no longer signs you in, so a mail
    client that previews links can't spend yours before you click.
    **Google** and **Apple** work too. If your account manages more than
    one venue, you pick which one after signing in — and once you're in,
    the header has a [venue switcher](/vendors/workspace/hub#switching-venues)
    for jumping between them.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="I lost my sign-in link.">
    Request a new one from the login page. Each link and code is
    one-time use: once a link is spent, re-opening it just shows a
    short "This link may have already been used" page. Grab a fresh
    one from `rumizi.com/login` and it works the same way.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="I invited a staff member by phone number and they can't sign in.">
    Fixed in the 2026-09-25 release. Older versions stored punctuated
    phone numbers (`+1 (555) 123-4567`) in a shape phone sign-in
    couldn't match, so the person was invited but never found by the
    login page. Rumizi has since normalized every stored phone number
    on record. Ask the staff member to try `rumizi.com/login` again —
    typing the number plain or formatted both work. If it still fails,
    open **More → Staff**, remove the row, and re-invite.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
